title: the HTML parse holds at most 512 open elements and closes the current one to make room, and every check it makes grows no faster than the document
scope:
how `Core\Html::parse` and `Core\Html::sanitize` bound the time one document can cost: a cap on the
stack of open elements, and three checks rewritten without changing their answer. It carries the
`html5ever` changes as a patched copy under `vendor/html5ever`. It does not change the memory limit,
which already bounds a tree's size, or `DEPTH_CEILING`, which bounds the walks over a finished tree.

summary.headline: Parsing HTML takes time in proportion to the document
summary.body: `Core\Html::parse` keeps at most 512 elements open at once, like the major browsers. When a document nests deeper, the next element closes the current one and becomes its sibling. No content is lost. Because of this limit, a small hostile document cannot keep a CPU core busy.
